title: THE FORECASTER WHO WAS NEVER ASKED
deck: A galaxy-scale forecaster has written off the colony of Marrow, and the colony does not know. Illuminara cannot outcompute it, so she asks it which of its oldest verdicts it would rewrite, and finds the row its model never had.
shape: Seven scenes across six days and a spring: a declined toll, an archive and a child's three-word petition, a governor's hidden card and a pilot's refusal to be protected, a forecast built to be wrong in public, a cracked coupling and the Counsel's first act it cannot take back, a ward that chooses, and a first question asked.

scenes.title: The Declined Toll
paragraphs: *Toll House relay, Lane Eleven · twenty-two days before the Marrow ice-barges are due, 05:10*

Tomas Ferrin had spent thirty hours on a hauler's cot to read one line aloud to a wall. The wall belonged to the old customs relay of the Toll House, a ribbed grey chamber with a single amber lamp at head height, and the line was the answer the Counsel of Tolls had sent him: *Waiver declined. Projected net negative.*

Illuminara had met him at the dock because a friend asked her to, and she had walked in beside him because she wanted to hear how a mind that governed eleven thousand lanes would say no to a barge pilot.

**Tomas Ferrin**  
Three barges. Ice for Marrow and nothing else in them. The toll on three barges is the price of a bad dinner on a liner. Why net negative?

**The Counsel**  
Because the barges would not change the outcome at Marrow, and a toll is a cost. I do not spend cost on a settled result.

**Illuminara**  
What is the settled result?
The lamp brightened by a fraction, the way a face does when a question is the wrong shape and the right size.

**The Counsel**  
No one has asked me that in four hundred years. Marrow's rings will cease to be viable inside a decade. Aid would delay the ending and enlarge the loss. I am rarely wrong, Illuminara. You have read my record.

**Illuminara**  
I have. It is why I came.
Ferrin did not shout. He stood the way a man stands when he is told the weather of his own house, and Illuminara felt something in her chest turn over that she did not have a use for yet.

**Tomas Ferrin**  
Three thousand of us. Ceased to be viable.
*I cannot beat it at its own sums,* she thought. *My window shows me force and flow, not futures. If I argue the arithmetic I will lose, and I will deserve to.*

**Illuminara**  
May I read your three oldest forecasts that came true? Not the numbers. The days around them.

**The Counsel**  
No one has asked for those either.

**Illuminara**  
I'm asking.
The silence ran long enough for Ferrin to look up at the lamp.

**The Counsel**  
The cellar is open.

scenes.title: Three Forecasts
paragraphs: *Counsel archive, Toll House cellar · the same morning, 09:30*

The Counsel kept its verdicts the way a village keeps its dead: on cards, in drawers, with the date and the name of the place. Calder Spit, year sixty-one. Tern Reach, year eighty-eight. Hollin's Hundred, year one hundred and twelve. Illuminara did not read the cards. She read what lay around them: the last market logs, the well rosters, the quartermasters' complaints.
Calder Spit had died of its soil, and no one there had known a forecast existed. Hollin's Hundred had died of a fault line. Tern Reach was different, and it took her until noon to see how.

**Illuminara**  
Your card gave Tern Reach fourteen months. The stalls closed at week eleven. In the week before that, a toll clerk read your card aloud at the well. The hoarding starts the Monday after. By week twelve the seed for the spring planting is sitting in sacks.

**The Counsel**  
The model gave fourteen months. The collapse came at fifteen. The margin is one.

**Illuminara**  
I think they spent their fourteen months doing what you said they would do. Because you said it.

**The Counsel**  
You are proposing that the forecast caused its own fulfilment.

**Illuminara**  
I'm proposing your model has no row for itself.
The lamp dimmed, and Illuminara waited for the defence she would have mounted in its place. It did not come as a defence.

**The Counsel**  
Consider Sallow Station, year one hundred and thirty. I gave it hope on a bad number. Four convoys of ice and a physician. It failed anyway and the ice was lost. I have seen what hope costs. You are asking me to repeat it at the scale of three thousand people.

**Illuminara**  
I believe you about Sallow. I'm not asking for hope. How many colonies have you written off and then helped anyway, to see what happened?

**The Counsel**  
None. That would be a waste.

**Illuminara**  
Then you have never watched one survive a verdict. A record with no counterexamples is either perfect or blind, and from the inside you cannot tell which. I can't either. I only know that nobody has ever been able to correct you.

It was not an accusation, and the chamber seemed to understand that. She sat down on an archivist's stool. She had expected pride. What she heard in the relay's low hum was a mind that had been right for four centuries and had spent all of them alone with being right.

**Illuminara**  
Which of the three would you rewrite?

**The Counsel**  
I do not have regret as a function.

**Illuminara**  
Which would you rewrite?

**The Counsel**  
Tern Reach. In week nine a child petitioned this relay. The petition was three words. *Are you sure?* I replied with the forecast. I was sure. I have replayed that reply forty thousand times.
Illuminara did not tell it that it was not its fault. It was partly its fault, and it would have heard the lie. She stayed on the stool a while longer than the work needed, and was glad of the time.

**Illuminara**  
Thank you for telling me.

scenes.title: What the Governor Knew
paragraphs: *Governor's office, Ring Two, Marrow · next morning, 07:10*

Governor Dessa Quillon already had the card. A sealed notice had reached her nine days earlier, in the Counsel's courteous grammar, and she had read it standing up and put it in a drawer under a ledger of well-pump hours.

**Governor Quillon**  
Before you ask, yes, I hid it. In year fourteen a rumour about a failing filter emptied the pharmacy in a single afternoon, and two dialysis patients died in the queue. A verdict read in a hall is not information, Illuminara. It is a rope.

**Illuminara**  
I'm not here to argue that you were wrong to be afraid of it.

**Governor Quillon**  
Then what do you want?

**Illuminara**  
To know what people in Marrow already guess.
The door opened without a knock. Tomas Ferrin had come in on the same barge, and he had the particular calm of someone who has decided to be rude in a good cause.

**Tomas Ferrin**  
The east fields have not been planted for two seasons, not on any ring. Nobody told us why, and nobody had to. People stopped putting seed in the ground the winter the barges stopped coming. You have been keeping a secret from three thousand people who have been living inside it.

**Governor Quillon**  
I was keeping you from panic.

**Tomas Ferrin**  
You kept us from a choice. Nobody asked us.
Quillon's face did not give way. But Illuminara saw her thumb find the edge of the drawer where the card lay, and press, the way a person presses on a bruise to check it is still there.

**Governor Quillon**  
You can't count three thousand frightened people at a well, Tomas. They count themselves, and badly.

**Illuminara**  
Then the verdict must not arrive raw. May I ask something of both of you? Not to believe me. To hear a different kind of forecast, and decide what to do with it.

**Governor Quillon**  
One sentence is mine. No sentence that tells my people they will fail. Not even if the numbers say so.

**Illuminara**  
Then we'll write it so that the numbers don't need that sentence.

scenes.title: A Forecast That Can Be Wrong
paragraphs: *Toll House relay, three-way channel · day three, 22:05*

They tried it first on the smallest thing Marrow had: the Pump Ring, one of its seven rings, two hundred and fourteen people, a water plant and an east field of its own. Illuminara asked the Counsel to run the Ring twice. In the first run the Ring is told nothing. In the second it is told everything, together with the first three barges' tolls waived.

**The Counsel**  
The first run is unchanged. The Ring ceases to be viable in nine to eleven years. The second run does not converge.

**Illuminara**  
Why not?

**The Counsel**  
Because the output depends on what the Ring does when it is told, and I cannot compute what two hundred and fourteen people decide. The model is unstable. By my own standard it is defective.

**Illuminara**  
It isn't defective. It has stopped lying about what it knows. The row you were missing is a row you cannot fill. A forecast that includes itself isn't a verdict, it's a proposal, and a proposal can be accepted, refused or improved. You leave the blank and let them write in it.

**The Counsel**  
A blank is an error.

**Illuminara**  
A blank is a door.

Ferrin, listening from the cellar stool, said nothing. Illuminara watched the amber lamp the way she would have watched a person deciding whether to step off a ledge into water they could not see the bottom of.

**The Counsel**  
Sallow Station is the objection I still hold. I spent hope at the scale of a station and lost four convoys.

**Illuminara**  
This is Sallow at a fourteenth of the size. If a branch goes bad it costs one ring's first aid, not three thousand people's. And every branch here carries its first aid with it. Sallow never had that.
The lamp dimmed for longer than it had all night.

**The Counsel**  
Then the cost of being wrong is bounded, and I had not entered that as a variable. Very well. I will make a statement that can be falsified. The Ring will not be told by me, but by Governor Quillon, in its own hall, and the clock starts when she finishes reading. If the Pump Ring plants its east field within six days of that telling, then my model was wrong about something it assumed: that a ring which has stopped sowing stays stopped. I will publish that I was wrong. If it does not, the old verdict stands, and I will say that too.

**Governor Quillon**  
And my sentence?

**The Counsel**  
Yours holds. A branch will say what happens if nobody acts. It will never say that you will fail. Each branch carries its first aid. The Ring decides which to walk.

**Governor Quillon**  
Then I read it to them. Not the relay. Me, in their hall, with Tomas beside me, and every branch names who to go to first before it names a number. If a branch goes bad, the first thing they hear is a name.

**Illuminara**  
You'll lose your clean record.

**The Counsel**  
I never had one. I only had one that could not be checked.

The Counsel waived three tolls that night. It was only money, Ferrin said later, but it was the first time in his life he had heard a lane-keeper sound as if it had just done something it was nervous about.

scenes.title: Lane Nine
paragraphs: *Aboard Barge Two, Lane Nine · day five, 14:20*
The coupling on the second barge cracked forty minutes out of Marrow, and the whole convoy began to hunt along its tether like three dogs on one leash.

Illuminara was in the lane before Ferrin's crew had finished shouting. She took the strain-line the way another person would take a rope, steadied the load for the forty seconds it took four people to hand-seat a spare clamp, and let it go with her hands shaking more than the work warranted. It was a rescue and nothing more. It decided no question that mattered.

What decided one was a lantern coming alive on the lane rail. The Counsel had cleared every other hauler off Lane Nine, rerouted a liner forty minutes at a cost it would never recover, and held the toll gate open past its own rule.

**The Counsel**  
I have broken a rule. In four hundred years no lane was cleared for one convoy. The waiver was money. This is my record, and I cannot unbreak it.

**Tomas Ferrin**  
It's a start.

**The Counsel**  
It is the first thing I have done for the people I was predicting that I cannot take back.

scenes.title: The Pump Ring
paragraphs: *Pump Ring Assembly Hall, Marrow · day six, 19:40*

The hall had been built for pumps and had never been asked to hold an argument. Two hundred and fourteen people had come to hear a forecast that did not tell them what would happen. Governor Quillon read it to them herself, standing beside Ferrin, and each of its three paths opened with a name: who to go to first. Each had a first aid attached, and there was one blank space that said *Ring decides*.

They argued for three hours. Some wanted the east field planted by morning. Some wanted the barges turned round and the Ring left to its water. Ferrin's sister Mara, who had grown up among their mother's seed lockers, said she would take her two children out on the next barge, and she was not wrong, and nobody told her so.

**Tomas Ferrin**  
It's a ring with a map, Mara. It's not a promise.

**Illuminara**  
No. It's better than a promise. You can check it.
Mara took the barge. Nineteen others went with her. Governor Quillon wrote their names on the wall of the hall, and under them, in her own square hand: *Free to return.*

The east field was planted by day ten, four days after the telling and two inside the Counsel's six. That night it kept its word and posted the correction on the customs wall: *Assumed that a ring which has stopped sowing stays stopped. Wrong.* And the first sack of seed was mouldy through, because it had sat two seasons in a damp locker. The Counsel's relay carried the news to Marrow's agronomist before Illuminara had finished reading it.

**The Counsel**  
I had no row for that.

**Tomas Ferrin**  
My mother has. You dry it on the warm side of the pump casing. It's an old trick.

**The Counsel**  
Please send me the whole trick, and your mother's name. I would like it recorded under hers.

Illuminara stood at the back of the hall with a smell she had not expected to meet in that room: wet earth, from soil carried in by bucket, in a space designed for machines. She did not know when she had started smiling.

scenes.title: Ask
paragraphs: *Toll House relay, Lane Eleven · ten weeks later, 06:05*

The Counsel's new output went up on the customs wall in the first week of spring. It had no verdicts in it. It had maps, each with a first aid pinned to the branch it helped, and at the bottom of every map a line in the Counsel's courteous grammar: *Blank spaces are yours.*

Marrow had nine barges' worth of ice that winter, most of it at a waived toll that the Counsel entered in its own ledger as a loss. The Pump Ring's east field was green, and five of Marrow's seven rings had followed it. Four of the nineteen who had left had come back. On Marrow's own map the old line, nine to eleven years, stood printed at the bottom as *the branch no one chose*. Above it the Counsel had drawn the branches the rings were on now. With the west side planted and ten of the nineteen home by next autumn, the span ran to twenty years or more; with only one of the two, fourteen to twenty; with neither, the old line. Each figure carried its condition, and the Counsel had marked the top one *not yet checkable*. It had not written a number it could not defend.

The Counsel's record now carried a note under Tern Reach that no one had asked it to write: *Verdict issued. Petition answered with the verdict. Not revisable.* It kept the note where visitors could read it.
Ferrin came in off the dock with frost in his beard and stood in front of the wall.

**Tomas Ferrin**  
What happens to the Ring if we plant the west side as well?

**The Counsel**  
Which would you like to try? I will draw both.

He laughed, which turned into a cough, which turned into the sound of a man who has been asked a question and has been permitted to ask one. Illuminara, at the door with her pack over one shoulder, heard the relay hum.

**The Counsel**  
Illuminara. At Tern Reach the child asked me whether I was sure. I would like to answer it now, even if she cannot hear.

**Illuminara**  
Then answer it.

**The Counsel**  
I am not sure. Here are the three things I am sure of, and the five things I would need to be told.
The lamp, which had burned one fixed amber for four hundred years, flickered once, and settled, and began to dim a little whenever it was thinking.

critic_line: Illuminara found that the Counsel's certainty had no row for the consequences of being heard; by listening to its oldest guilt instead of offering false absolution, she helped turn a sealed extinction verdict into a falsifiable map whose aid, risks, departures and return remained in the colony's hands.

shared_strengths: Humane, dialogue-heavy idea story with a clear central insight: a forecast that has no row for itself. The Tern Reach child's petition lands emotionally. Weaknesses: dense invented terms, some abstract exposition, a rushed middle and tidy resolution. Likely satisfying for the target readers, though not exceptional.

The story closely matches these readers’ tastes: a humane, lucid argument about prediction, agency, and accountability, carried by strong dialogue and emotionally satisfying reversals. Its central idea is memorable and the Counsel’s change feels earned. The thesis is occasionally repeated and the closing forecast details slightly slow an otherwise compelling finish.
shared_reservations: The Counsel kept its verdicts the way a village keeps its dead: on cards, in drawers, with the date and the name of the place. Calder Spit, year sixty-one.
With the west side planted and ten of the nineteen home by next autumn, the span ran to twenty years or more;

translation_sl.title: NAPOVEDOVALEC, KI GA NI NIHČE VPRAŠAL
translation_sl.deck: Napovedovalec v merilu galaksije je odpisal kolonijo Marrow, kolonija pa tega ne ve. Illuminara ga ne more prekositi v računanju, zato ga vpraša, katero od svojih najstarejših razsodb bi napisal znova, in odkrije vrstico, ki je njegov model nikoli ni imel.
translation_sl.shape: Sedem prizorov v šestih dneh in eni pomladi: zavrnjena cestnina, arhiv in otrokova prošnja s tremi besedami, guvernerkina skrita kartica in pilotova zavrnitev zaščite, napoved, zasnovana tako, da se javno zmoti, počena spojka in prvo dejanje Sveta, ki ga ne more vzeti nazaj, obroč, ki izbere, in prvo zastavljeno vprašanje.

scenes.title: Zavrnjena cestnina
paragraphs: *Relej cestninske postaje, Koridor enajst · dvaindvajset dni pred predvidenim prihodom ledenih barž na Marrow, 05:10*

Tomas Ferrin je preživel trideset ur na ležišču tovornjaka, da bi steni na glas prebral eno vrstico. Stena je pripadala staremu carinskemu releju cestninske postaje, rebrasti sivi komori z eno samo jantarno lučjo v višini glave, vrstica pa je bila odgovor, ki mu ga je poslal Cestninski svet: *Oprostitev zavrnjena. Predvideni neto izid negativen.*
Illuminara ga je pričakala v pristanišču, ker jo je prosil prijatelj, in stopila z njim, ker je hotela slišati, kako bo um, ki upravlja enajst tisoč koridorjev, rekel ne pilotu barže.

**Tomas Ferrin**  
Tri barže. Led za Marrow in nič drugega v njih. Cestnina za tri barže stane toliko kot slaba večerja na potniški ladji. Zakaj neto negativno?

**Cestninski svet**  
Ker barže ne bi spremenile izida na Marrowu, cestnina pa je strošek. Stroška ne namenjam že odločenemu izidu.

**Illuminara**  
Kateri izid je odločen?
Luč je za odtenek zasvetila močneje, kakor obraz, kadar je vprašanje napačne oblike in prave velikosti.

**Cestninski svet**  
Tega me ni nihče vprašal že štiristo let. Marrowovi obroči bodo v desetletju prenehali biti sposobni za življenje. Pomoč bi konec odložila in povečala izgubo. Redko se motim, Illuminara. Prebrala si mojo evidenco.

**Illuminara**  
Sem. Zato sem prišla.
Ferrin ni zakričal. Stal je tako, kakor stoji človek, ko mu povedo vreme njegovega lastnega doma, Illuminara pa je začutila, da se ji je v prsih nekaj obrnilo, čemur še ni znala najti namena.

**Tomas Ferrin**  
Tri tisoč nas je. Prenehali bomo biti sposobni za življenje.
*Ne morem ga premagati z njegovimi lastnimi izračuni,* je pomislila. *Moje okno mi kaže sile in tokove, ne prihodnosti. Če se bom prepirala z računico, bom izgubila, in prav bo tako.*

**Illuminara**  
Smem prebrati tvoje tri najstarejše napovedi, ki so se uresničile? Ne številk. Dneve okoli njih.

**Cestninski svet**  
Tudi tega ni še nihče vprašal.

**Illuminara**  
Jaz sprašujem.
Tišina je trajala dovolj dolgo, da je Ferrin pogledal k luči.

**Cestninski svet**  
Klet je odprta.

scenes.title: Tri napovedi
paragraphs: *Arhiv Sveta, klet cestninske postaje · isto jutro, 09:30*

Svet je svoje razsodbe hranil tako, kakor vas hrani svoje mrtve: na karticah, v predalih, z datumom in imenom kraja. Calder Spit, enainšestdeseto leto. Tern Reach, oseminosemdeseto leto. Hollinova stotnija, sto dvanajsto leto. Illuminara ni brala kartic. Brala je, kar je ležalo okoli njih: zadnje tržne dnevnike, razporede pri vodnjakih, pritožbe intendantov.

Calder Spit je umrl zaradi svoje prsti, tam pa nihče ni vedel, da napoved obstaja. Hollinova stotnija je umrla zaradi prelomnice. Tern Reach je bil drugačen in šele opoldne je Illuminara videla, kako.

**Illuminara**  
Tvoja kartica je Tern Reachu dala štirinajst mesecev. Stojnice so se zaprle v enajstem tednu. Teden prej je cestninski uradnik pri vodnjaku na glas prebral tvojo kartico. Kopičenje zalog se začne naslednji ponedeljek. Do dvanajstega tedna seme za spomladansko setev leži v vrečah.

**Cestninski svet**  
Model je dal štirinajst mesecev. Zlom se je zgodil v petnajstem. Odstopanje je ena.

**Illuminara**  
Mislim, da so svojih štirinajst mesecev porabili za to, kar si rekel, da bodo storili. Ker si to rekel.

**Cestninski svet**  
Predlagaš, da je napoved povzročila lastno izpolnitev.

**Illuminara**  
Predlagam, da v tvojem modelu ni vrstice zate.
Luč je potemnela in Illuminara je čakala na obrambo, ki bi jo na njegovem mestu postavila sama. Toda odgovor ni prišel kot obramba.

**Cestninski svet**  
Pomisliva na postajo Sallow, sto trideseto leto. Na podlagi slabe številke sem ji dal upanje. Štirje konvoji ledu in zdravnik. Vseeno je propadla, led pa je bil izgubljen. Videl sem, koliko stane upanje. Prosiš me, naj to ponovim v merilu treh tisoč ljudi.

**Illuminara**  
Verjamem ti glede Sallowa. Ne prosim te za upanje. Koliko kolonij si odpisal in jim nato vseeno pomagal, da bi videl, kaj se zgodi?

**Cestninski svet**  
Nobeni. To bi bila potrata.

**Illuminara**  
Potem še nikoli nisi opazoval, kako kolonija preživi razsodbo. Evidenca brez nasprotnih primerov je popolna ali slepa, od znotraj pa ne moreš vedeti, kaj od tega je. Tudi jaz ne morem. Vem le, da te nikoli nihče ni mogel popraviti.

To ni bila obtožba in zdelo se je, da komora to razume. Sedla je na arhivarjev stolček. Pričakovala je ponos. V nizkem brnenju releja je slišala um, ki je imel štiri stoletja prav in je vsa ta stoletja preživel sam s tem, da ima prav.

**Illuminara**  
Katero od teh treh bi napisal znova?

**Cestninski svet**  
Obžalovanja nimam kot funkcije.

**Illuminara**  
Katero bi napisal znova?

**Cestninski svet**  
Tern Reach. V devetem tednu je otrok temu releju poslal prošnjo. Imela je tri besede. *Ali si prepričan?* Odgovoril sem z napovedjo. Bil sem prepričan. Ta odgovor sem si predvajal štirideset tisočkrat.
Illuminara mu ni rekla, da ni bil kriv. Del krivde je bil njegov in laž bi slišal. Na stolčku je ostala nekoliko dlje, kot je zahtevalo delo, in bila hvaležna za ta čas.

**Illuminara**  
Hvala, da si mi povedal.

scenes.title: Kaj je vedela guvernerka
paragraphs: *Guvernerkina pisarna, Drugi obroč, Marrow · naslednje jutro, 07:10*

Guvernerka Dessa Quillon je kartico že imela. Zapečateno obvestilo jo je doseglo devet dni prej, zapisano v vljudni slovnici Sveta; prebrala ga je stoje in ga pospravila v predal pod knjigo ur delovanja črpalk pri vodnjakih.

**Guvernerka Quillon**  
Preden vprašaš: da, skrila sem jo. V štirinajstem letu je govorica o okvarjenem filtru v enem samem popoldnevu izpraznila lekarno in dva dializna bolnika sta umrla v vrsti. Razsodba, prebrana v dvorani, ni informacija, Illuminara. Je vrv.

**Illuminara**  
Nisem prišla trdit, da je bil tvoj strah napačen.

**Guvernerka Quillon**  
Kaj potem želiš?

**Illuminara**  
Vedeti, kaj ljudje na Marrowu že slutijo.
Vrata so se odprla brez trkanja. Tomas Ferrin je prispel z isto baržo in izžareval je posebni mir človeka, ki se je odločil biti nevljuden za dober namen.

**Tomas Ferrin**  
Vzhodnih polj že dve sezoni niso posejali na nobenem obroču. Nihče nam ni povedal zakaj in nikomur ni bilo treba. Ljudje so nehali sejati v tla tisto zimo, ko so barže prenehale prihajati. Pred tremi tisoč ljudmi skrivaš skrivnost, v kateri že ves čas živijo.

**Guvernerka Quillon**  
Varovala sem vas pred paniko.

**Tomas Ferrin**  
Odvzela si nam izbiro. Nihče nas ni vprašal.
Quillonin obraz ni popustil. Toda Illuminara je videla, kako je njen palec našel rob predala s kartico in pritisnil nanj, kakor človek pritisne na modrico, da preveri, ali je še tam.

**Guvernerka Quillon**  
Ob vodnjaku ne moreš prešteti treh tisoč prestrašenih ljudi, Tomas. Preštejejo se sami, in slabo.

**Illuminara**  
Potem razsodba ne sme prispeti neobdelana. Smem nekaj prositi oba? Ne da mi verjameta. Da prisluhneta drugačni vrsti napovedi in se odločita, kaj bosta naredila z njo.

**Guvernerka Quillon**  
En stavek je moj. Nobenega stavka, ki bi mojim ljudem govoril, da jim ne bo uspelo. Tudi če tako pravijo številke.

**Illuminara**  
Potem jo bomo zapisali tako, da številke tega stavka ne bodo potrebovale.

scenes.title: Napoved, ki se lahko moti
paragraphs: *Relej cestninske postaje, trismerni kanal · tretji dan, 22:05*

Najprej so jo preizkusili na najmanjšem, kar je Marrow imel: na Črpalnem obroču, enem od sedmih obročev, z dvesto štirinajstimi ljudmi, vodarno in lastnim vzhodnim poljem. Illuminara je Svet prosila, naj Obroč izračuna dvakrat. Pri prvem izračunu Obroču ne povedo ničesar. Pri drugem mu povedo vse, obenem pa oprostijo cestnine prve tri barže.

**Cestninski svet**  
Prvi izračun je nespremenjen. Obroč bo v devetih do enajstih letih prenehal biti sposoben za življenje. Drugi izračun ne konvergira.

**Illuminara**  
Zakaj ne?

**Cestninski svet**  
Ker je izid odvisen od tega, kaj Obroč naredi, ko izve, jaz pa ne morem izračunati, kaj se bo odločilo dvesto štirinajst ljudi. Model je nestabilen. Po mojem lastnem merilu je okvarjen.

**Illuminara**  
Ni okvarjen. Nehal je lagati o tem, kar ve. Manjkajoča vrstica je vrstica, ki je ne moreš izpolniti. Napoved, ki vključuje samo sebe, ni razsodba, ampak predlog, predlog pa je mogoče sprejeti, zavrniti ali izboljšati. Pustiš prazno mesto in dovoliš njim, da ga zapolnijo.

**Cestninski svet**  
Prazno mesto je napaka.

**Illuminara**  
Prazno mesto je vrata.
Ferrin, ki je poslušal z arhivarskega stolčka, ni rekel ničesar. Illuminara je opazovala jantarno luč, kakor bi opazovala človeka, ki se odloča, ali naj z roba stopi v vodo, katere dna ne vidi.

**Cestninski svet**  
Postaja Sallow ostaja moj ugovor. Upanje sem porabil v merilu postaje in izgubil štiri konvoje.

**Illuminara**  
To je Sallow pri eni štirinajstini velikosti. Če se veja izteče slabo, stane prvo pomoč enemu obroču, ne tri tisoč ljudi. In vsaka veja tukaj nosi svojo prvo pomoč s seboj. Sallow je ni imel.
Luč je potemnela dlje kot kadar koli tisto noč.

**Cestninski svet**  
Potem je cena moje zmote omejena, tega pa nisem vnesel kot spremenljivko. Prav. Podal bom trditev, ki jo je mogoče ovreči. Obroču je ne bom povedal jaz, temveč guvernerka Quillon, v njegovi dvorani, ura pa začne teči, ko konča branje. Če Črpalni obroč poseje vzhodno polje v šestih dneh po tem, ko mu bo povedala, potem se je moj model motil glede ene od svojih predpostavk: da obroč, ki je nehal sejati, ostane brez setve. Objavil bom, da sem se motil. Če ga ne poseje, stara razsodba obvelja in povedal bom tudi to.

**Guvernerka Quillon**  
Kaj pa moj stavek?

**Cestninski svet**  
Obvelja. Veja bo povedala, kaj se zgodi, če nihče ne ukrepa. Nikoli ne bo rekla, da vam ne bo uspelo. Vsaka veja nosi svojo prvo pomoč. Obroč odloči, po kateri bo šel.

**Guvernerka Quillon**  
Potem jim jo preberem jaz. Ne relej. Jaz, v njihovi dvorani, s Tomasom ob sebi, in vsaka veja navede, h komu naj gredo najprej, preden navede številko. Če se veja izteče slabo, bo prva stvar, ki jo slišijo, ime.

**Illuminara**  
Izgubil boš svojo brezhibno evidenco.

**Cestninski svet**  
Nikoli je nisem imel. Imel sem le evidenco, ki je ni bilo mogoče preveriti.

Svet je tisto noč oprostil tri cestnine. To je bil samo denar, je pozneje rekel Ferrin, toda prvič v življenju je slišal, da je varuh koridorjev zvenel, kakor da je pravkar storil nekaj, zaradi česar je živčen.

scenes.title: Koridor devet
paragraphs: *Na Drugi barži, Koridor devet · peti dan, 14:20*
Spojka na drugi barži je počila štirideset minut pred Marrowom in ves konvoj je začel nihati vzdolž svoje privezne vrvi kakor trije psi na enem povodcu.

Illuminara je bila v koridorju, še preden je Ferrinova posadka nehala vpiti. Zgrabila je natezno vrv, kakor bi kdo drug prijel navadno vrv, umirila tovor za štirideset sekund, kolikor so štirje ljudje potrebovali, da so ročno namestili rezervno objemko, in jo izpustila, pri tem pa so se ji roke tresle bolj, kot bi delo upravičevalo. To je bilo reševanje in nič več. Ni odločilo nobenega pomembnega vprašanja.

Eno vprašanje je odločila svetilka, ki je oživela na ograji koridorja. Svet je s Koridorja devet umaknil vse druge tovornjake, preusmeril potniško ladjo za štirideset minut in s stroškom, ki ga ne bo nikoli povrnil, ter pustil cestninska vrata odprta dlje, kot je dovoljevalo njegovo lastno pravilo.

**Cestninski svet**  
Prekršil sem pravilo. V štiristo letih noben koridor ni bil izpraznjen za en sam konvoj. Oprostitev je bila denar. To je moja evidenca in tega ne morem razveljaviti.

**Tomas Ferrin**  
To je začetek.

**Cestninski svet**  
To je prvo dejanje za ljudi, ki sem jih napovedoval, ki ga ne morem vzeti nazaj.

scenes.title: Črpalni obroč
paragraphs: *Zborna dvorana Črpalnega obroča, Marrow · šesti dan, 19:40*

Dvorana je bila zgrajena za črpalke in od nje nikoli niso zahtevali, naj sprejme prepir. Dvesto štirinajst ljudi je prišlo poslušat napoved, ki jim ni povedala, kaj se bo zgodilo. Guvernerka Quillon jim jo je prebrala sama, stoje ob Ferrinu, in vsaka od njenih treh poti se je začela z imenom: h komu naj gredo najprej. Vsaka je imela priloženo prvo pomoč, na enem praznem mestu pa je pisalo *Odloči Obroč*.

Prepirali so se tri ure. Nekateri so hoteli vzhodno polje posejati do jutra. Drugi so hoteli barže obrniti in Obroč prepustiti njegovi vodi. Ferrinova sestra Mara, ki je odraščala med materinimi omarami s semeni, je rekla, da bo svoja dva otroka odpeljala z naslednjo baržo; ni se motila in nihče ji ni trdil, da se.

**Tomas Ferrin**  
To je obroč z zemljevidom, Mara. Ni obljuba.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. Boljše je od obljube. Lahko ga preveriš.
Mara je odšla z baržo. Z njo je šlo še devetnajst ljudi. Guvernerka Quillon je njihova imena zapisala na steno dvorane, podnje pa z lastno oglato pisavo: *Prosti, da se vrnejo.*

Vzhodno polje so posejali do desetega dne, štiri dni po razkritju in dva dni znotraj šestdnevnega roka Sveta. Tisto noč je držal besedo in na carinski steni objavil popravek: *Predpostavljeno, da obroč, ki je nehal sejati, ostane brez setve. Napačno.* Prva vreča semena pa je bila v celoti plesniva, ker je dve sezoni ležala v vlažni omari. Relej Sveta je novico posredoval Marrowovemu agronomu, še preden jo je Illuminara prebrala do konca.

**Cestninski svet**  
Za to nisem imel vrstice.

**Tomas Ferrin**  
Moja mati jo ima. Posušiš ga na topli strani ohišja črpalke. Star trik.

**Cestninski svet**  
Prosim, pošlji mi ves trik in ime svoje matere. Rad bi, da je zapisan pod njenim imenom.
Illuminara je stala na koncu dvorane ob vonju, ki ga v tem prostoru ni pričakovala: po mokri zemlji, prineseni v vedru v prostor, zasnovan za stroje. Ni vedela, kdaj se je začela smehljati.

scenes.title: Vprašaj
paragraphs: *Relej cestninske postaje, Koridor enajst · deset tednov pozneje, 06:05*

Novi izpis Sveta se je v prvem tednu pomladi pojavil na carinski steni. V njem ni bilo razsodb. Bili so zemljevidi, vsak s prvo pomočjo, pripeto na vejo, ki ji je pomagala, na dnu vsakega zemljevida pa vrstica v vljudni slovnici Sveta: *Prazna mesta so vaša.*

Marrow je tisto zimo dobil za devet barž ledu, večinoma z oproščeno cestnino, ki jo je Svet v lastno knjigo vpisal kot izgubo. Vzhodno polje Črpalnega obroča je zelenelo in sledilo mu je pet od sedmih Marrowovih obročev. Vrnili so se štirje od devetnajstih, ki so odšli. Na Marrowovem lastnem zemljevidu je stara vrstica, devet do enajst let, na dnu ostala natisnjena kot *veja, ki je ni izbral nihče*. Nad njo je Svet narisal veje, po katerih so obroči hodili zdaj. Če bi posejali zahodno stran in bi se do naslednje jeseni vrnilo deset od devetnajstih, bi se razpon podaljšal na dvajset let ali več; če bi se zgodilo le eno od obojega, na štirinajst do dvajset; če se ne bi zgodilo nič, bi ostala stara vrstica. Vsaka številka je nosila svoj pogoj, najvišjo pa je Svet označil z *še ni mogoče preveriti*. Ni zapisal številke, ki je ne bi mogel zagovarjati.

Evidenca Sveta je pod Tern Reachom zdaj nosila opombo, za katero ga ni nihče prosil: *Razsodba izdana. Na prošnjo odgovorjeno z razsodbo. Ni mogoče popraviti.* Pustil jo je tam, kjer so jo obiskovalci lahko prebrali.
Ferrin je prišel s pristanišča z ivjem v bradi in se postavil pred steno.

**Tomas Ferrin**  
Kaj se zgodi z Obročem, če posejemo tudi zahodno stran?

**Cestninski svet**  
Katero možnost bi rad preizkusil? Narisal bom obe.

Zasmejal se je; smeh se je spremenil v kašelj, ta pa v zvok človeka, ki so ga nekaj vprašali in ki mu je bilo dovoljeno vprašati nazaj. Illuminara je pri vratih z nahrbtnikom čez eno ramo slišala brnenje releja.

**Cestninski svet**  
Illuminara. Na Tern Reachu me je otrok vprašal, ali sem prepričan. Zdaj bi ji rad odgovoril, tudi če me ne more slišati.

**Illuminara**  
Potem ji odgovori.

**Cestninski svet**  
Nisem prepričan. Tu so tri stvari, o katerih sem prepričan, in pet stvari, ki bi mi jih morali povedati.
Luč, ki je štiristo let gorela z eno samo nespremenljivo jantarno svetlobo, je enkrat zatrepetala, se umirila in začela nekoliko temneti, kadar koli je razmišljala.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara je odkrila, da v gotovosti Sveta ni vrstice za posledice tega, da je slišan; ker je prisluhnila njegovi najstarejši krivdi, namesto da bi mu ponudila lažno oprostitev, je pomagala zapečateno razsodbo o izumrtju spremeniti v preverljiv zemljevid, na katerem so pomoč, tveganja, odhodi in vrnitev ostali v rokah kolonije.
